short_answer: Jimmy Boyd runs a real, working pick business. His site names an operator, publishes every price, takes payment through a SportsCapping checkout, and posts a dated archive of his graded picks, losses included. In that narrow sense he is legitimate.

The record is not independent. SportsCapping grades, ranks and sells his picks, and its own help page now says Boyd Information Group, the company on the BoydsBets contact page, is "the company behind SportsCapping.com". His FAQ still calls this documentation by "independent sports monitors". On the network's own numbers he is a small winner over a long stretch: 5,855 wins and 5,324 losses since January 2018, 52.4%, with profit of about 1.7 cents for every dollar risked.

We checked six of his sales runs against that archive. Two matched exactly, and four did not: his NBA page claims a 10 and 6 run over his last 16 picks while the archive showed 6 and 10. Treat the archive as useful raw data from the seller, not as an audit. If you buy, buy short, record every pick yourself with the line you got, and judge it after a few hundred picks.

guarantee: The SportsCapping guarantee page was rewritten since our last check. It now reads: "A guaranteed purchase triggers its guarantee when the picks it covers finish with a total profit of zero or less, breaking even counts." For a losing package, "you automatically receive the handicapper's next day of picks in the same sport, free." A guaranteed subscription that does not profit "is automatically extended by its original length." Nothing has to be claimed. Some accounts get account credit for the amount paid instead.

The limits are in "The Fine Print": "Season and rest-of-season passes are not guaranteed", "Replacement picks and extensions don't carry a guarantee of their own" and "Guarantees apply once per purchase." Credits "can't be withdrawn or exchanged for cash." On refunds, the SportsCapping help page now says "Because picks are graded results, refunds are reviewed individually", a softer line than the "We do not offer monetary refunds" wording we read on 7 Nov. In the one BBB complaint, the business offered a partial or full refund. Losses on your own bets are never covered.

claims_note: How we checked: on 20 Nov 2026 we opened his SportsCapping archive filtered to each sport (NFL, college football, NBA, college basketball and football top plays), took the most recent 120 picks for each, sorted them by pick date, dropped pushes and counted back. Profit is the archive's own figure at $100 a pick, after the juice. Picks released on the same day can sort in a slightly different order, so a run can differ by a pick at its edge. Two runs matched exactly. Four did not come close, and one, the NBA run, was the reverse of what the archive showed.

The college basketball claims are the hardest to square. A run over the last 100 college basketball picks needs at least 100 graded picks, and the archive held 79 for that sport, all since 17 Mar 2026. The figures may come from an older record that the network no longer shows, but a buyer has no way to see it.

"Dime bettors" means $1,000 a pick, ten times the archive's $100, so every dollar figure in his sales copy is ten times the archive figure. The page also sells off season products: on 20 Nov 2026 a WNBA pass was still for sale through 1 Dec and an MLB pass was listed weeks after the World Series.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing complete. We found no pick log kept by a grader with no tie to the seller, and no court or regulator record about Jimmy Boyd or Boyd Information Group.

What the seller's network publishes: SportsCapping shows a Jimmy Boyd archive with the date, pick, line, odds, score, result and profit for each pick, losses included. On 20 Nov 2026 its all sports row read 5,855 wins and 5,324 losses since 20 Jan 2018, with 240 pushes, 52.4%, +$20,532.50 at $100 a pick and a return of 1.65% of money risked. His top plays row read 2,813 and 2,542 since 12 Aug 2017, 52.5%. By sport, MLB (1,497 and 1,313, +$17,841 since 2017) carries most of the profit; NBA (+$14 since March 2025), NHL (+$208 since 2019) and college football (+$1,624 since 2012) are close to flat.

Put in a buyer's terms: 20 Jan 2018 to 19 Nov 2026 is about 8.8 years, so the archive's profit averages about $2,300 a year at $100 a pick. A 365 day pass costs $1,999.95. At $100 a pick, the pass would have taken almost all of the average year's profit, before any line you got that was worse than his.

Recent form: his page showed 63 wins and 54 losses over the last 30 days, +$424, ranked 22nd. On the network's 2026 all sports leaderboard he was not among the 31 handicappers listed. Ownership: the SportsCapping help page answers "Why is there a charge from Boyd Information Group on my statement?" with "Boyd Information Group is the company behind SportsCapping.com". That settles the question our earlier edition left open: the grader and the seller list the same company.

our_data.text: Watchdog grades picks captured from public posts before the game starts. In this edition Jimmy Boyd is not matched to a Watchdog graded record, so we make no claim about how his picks perform.
our_data.context: For scale: his SportsCapping all sports row since 20 Jan 2018 shows 52.4% winners. On the Watchdog board on 20 Nov 2026, {{over60}} of {{established}} established accounts (100 or more graded picks) were at 60% or better, and the median established account won {{median_win}}% of its picks. At standard -110 odds a bettor needs about 52.4% to break even.

customers_intro: Independent customer evidence on Jimmy Boyd is thin and mostly old. We found one BBB complaint, nine buyer comments from 2013 to 2017 on HandicappingReviews.org that lean negative, a few TheRX posts, and a comment section on a review site that belongs to his own sales network. Below is everything we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We found about a dozen buyer accounts across BBB, HandicappingReviews.org and TheRX, spread from 2013 to 2026. The older ones repeat two points: results near or below break even, and poor contact, with emails unanswered and sales calls that would not stop. Two of the 2015 and 2016 reviewers also said they never saw him on the network leaderboard, which matches what we saw in 2026. The newest complaint, to BBB in September 2026, was about a paid season pass that was never switched on; the business fixed it and offered a refund, and the buyer accepted. On the positive side, a TheRX member said in February 2026 that Boyd rescued his baseball season, which fits the archive, where MLB is his strongest sport. Praise on Capper Reviews comes from a site inside his own sales network. No buyer posted a full record of what he received.

A buyer told the BBB that a season pass bought for $399.95 on 5 Sep 2026 was never activated and that four or five emails got no reply. The business answered that a system fault had recorded the order without turning the pass on, that it activated the pass on 29 Sep backdated to the purchase, and that it offered a partial or full refund. BBB lists the complaint as resolved; the customer called the answer satisfactory on 30 Sep 2026.

BBB lists Boyd Information Group as a sports handicapper, not accredited and not rated because it "has been in business less than 6 months" by BBB's file, which was opened on 9/29/2026, with 1 complaint in the last 3 years. A new file means BBB has little history to go on either way.

His sales copy says clients "return each fall" and that more members return to his service every year than any other. These are the seller's own words, with no customer named, so they tell you nothing about a typical buyer.
On HandicappingReviews.org, a reviewer said he used the service for a while, that it was never above 50 percent, and that his emails got no reply. He said he would not use it again.
Another HandicappingReviews.org reviewer said every pick he received had lost and that the losses were putting his rent at risk. He posted no record of the picks.
A reviewer on the same page said the picks did well at first and then got worse, leaving him about break even, and that he would keep using the service to see how it went.
A reviewer said he bought about a month of picks and found them only slightly better than picking at random. He called the service OK and "not bad", while saying better options might exist.
A reviewer complained that the business kept calling his cell phone after he had asked many times for the calls to stop. He did not say whether he had bought picks.

Capper Reviews, which says it is part of the SportsCapping network that sells Boyd's picks, shows a 3.53 out of 5 rating from 49 votes and 9 undated comments. Most praise his consistency, write ups and a college basketball run, while two complain about a losing pick and a bad first day. Because the site belongs to the seller's own network, we give these comments little weight.
CapperTek's customer review page for BoydsBets.com showed no reviews or complaints.
In a TheRX service play thread, a member asked whether anyone had used Jimmy Boyd and whether he was worth switching to. No one on that page answered the question.

Trustpilot showed no page for boydsbets.com or sportscapping.com. In the Reddit betting forum posts we could search through the Arctic Shift archive on 20 Nov 2026, BoydsBets appeared only as a link to its articles on key numbers and trends, never as a pick service someone had bought. Several archive comment searches timed out, so a Reddit comment about him could be missing. Sportsbook Review forum threads from 2012 that mention him would not open for us, so we do not report them.

On HandicappingReviews.org, a reviewer said his experience had been miserable, that the records on the site must be fake because his results were the opposite, that the site was hard to use, and that he had lost money following the picks.
Another reviewer said he used Boyd a few years earlier and the picks were heavy losers, and that following him on SportsCapping he never saw Boyd on the leaderboard.
A reviewer called the service awful, said Boyd ranked 13th on his own network's site, and claimed the picks looked copied from ESPN's pick center. He gave no evidence for that last point.
A reviewer said he stayed with the service for a few years and lost consistently, and lost more when he bought the specials. He said the picks seemed random.

In a TheRX service plays discussion thread, a member said he had given up on another handicapper during the baseball season, had a strong football season with a third, and that Jimmy Boyd "ended up rescuing baseball season". He posted no record.

conflicts: The biggest one is the grader. SportsCapping.com grades and ranks Boyd's picks, sells them and runs his checkout, and its help page says Boyd Information Group, the company on the BoydsBets contact page, is "the company behind SportsCapping.com". A buyer should treat SportsCapping's archive, leaderboards and top 10 finishes as the seller's own record, not an outside audit.

BoydsBets also sells picks from other handicappers through the same checkout, and SportsCapping sells dozens more. The network earns from a whole roster, so it has a reason to promote whoever is hot this month.

His FAQ says a free trial is offered "only if you sign up for one of our recommended sportsbooks and make a deposit." The sportsbook page ranks offshore books such as BetOnline, Bovada and Bookmaker, and the FAQ says his posted line comes from "a variety of offshore books." Tying a trial to a deposit shows an interest in where you bet. Offshore sportsbooks are not licensed by U.S. state regulators. Check the law where you live.
strengths: A named operator, an address, a working checkout and a full public price list.
A dated pick archive with the line, odds, result and profit for every graded pick, losses included, going back to 2018 for all sports. Few sellers show that much.
Two of the six sales runs we checked matched the archive exactly, including the NFL 35 and 25 run.

The rewritten guarantee counts a break even day as a loss, applies itself without a claim, and the help page now allows refunds case by case. The one BBB complaint was fixed within a day of filing with a refund offer.
Free picks with a full written case are posted daily, so a reader can judge his reasoning before paying.
concerns: The only full record is published by a network that names Boyd Information Group as the company behind it, while his FAQ calls it independent.
Four of the six sales runs we checked did not match the archive, and the NBA run was the reverse of it (claimed 10 and 6, archive 6 and 10).
Over 8.8 years the archive shows a thin edge, about 1.7 cents per dollar risked, which a year pass at $1,999.95 would mostly use up at $100 a pick.
Season passes carry no guarantee, and WNBA and MLB passes were still for sale after those seasons ended.
Sales copy contradicts itself on years in business, and dollar figures assume $1,000 a pick.
Free trials are tied to depositing at a recommended offshore sportsbook.
checklist: Before you buy, open his archive for the sport you want and count the last 50 decided picks yourself. Compare it with the run in the sales copy.
Divide any "dime bettor" dollar figure by ten to get the figure at $100 a pick.
Add up what you would pay in a year and compare it with the archive's profit at your bet size. A small edge can be smaller than the subscription.
Read the guarantee badge on the exact package. Season and rest of season passes are not covered, and replacement days carry no guarantee of their own.
Write down each pick the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get, not the posted line.
Do not deposit at an offshore sportsbook to get a free trial.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He runs a real business with a named operator, a public price list, a working checkout and a dated pick archive, and BBB lists one complaint, resolved. What is not independent is the record: SportsCapping, which grades it, names Boyd Information Group as the company behind it.
How much does Jimmy Boyd cost?
On 20 Nov 2026 single best bets cost $29.99 to $74.96, day packs $49.97 to $99.97, all sports passes $99.95 for 3 days up to $1,999.95 for 365 days, and season passes $450 to $999.97.

On the network archive on 20 Nov 2026: 5,855 wins and 5,324 losses since January 2018, 52.4%, about 1.7 cents of profit per dollar risked at the posted lines. MLB carries most of the profit; NBA is close to flat.
Are his advertised win streaks accurate?

Some are. We checked six against his archive: the NFL 35 and 25 run and the college football 11 and 5 run matched. Two college football and college basketball runs did not, and the NBA 10 and 6 run showed as 6 and 10.

The help page says refunds are reviewed individually. Guaranteed packages that do not profit get the next day free, guaranteed subscriptions get extended, and season passes get nothing. In the one BBB complaint the business offered a refund.

On the seller's own numbers he has been a small long run winner, but the edge is thin enough that the price of a long pass can eat it at ordinary bet sizes. If you try him, buy short, keep your own record and compare it with the archive.
